subject.title: [Bug]: Memory Multimodal Indexing - Gemini API rejects OGG/Opus audio files

question: Should Gemini multimodal memory treat OGG/Opus as unsupported audio to skip/report, or should OpenClaw own automatic transcoding to MP3/WAV before embedding?
rationale: Both choices are technically plausible but have different compatibility, dependency, and maintenance costs, so automation should not choose the public memory audio contract.

options.title: Narrow Gemini Audio Support
options.body: Document and enforce MP3/WAV-only audio for Gemini embeddings, with a clear non-fatal skip or diagnostic for OGG/Opus files.

options.title: Own Transcoding
options.body: Add an ffmpeg-backed conversion path for unsupported audio formats before Gemini embedding, including dependency detection and failure handling.

options.title: Defer To Broader Multimodal Design
options.body: Keep this open under the broader multimodal memory direction until provider-specific media handling is settled across formats.

recommendation.title: Narrow Gemini Audio Support
recommendation.body: Document and enforce MP3/WAV-only audio for Gemini embeddings, with a clear non-fatal skip or diagnostic for OGG/Opus files.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision lands closest to the shipped multimodal memory extraPaths boundary and docs introduced through the merged multimodal memory work.
